title: Package freeze-safe Apple T1 Touch Bar driver
author: monomyth
body:
## Summary

Package the freeze-safe Apple T1 iBridge and firmware Touch Bar driver as `apple-ib-drv-dkms`.

- Uses the upstream `t1-touchbar` v0.3.0 release archive with a pinned SHA-256.
- Carries checksum-pinned resume and T1 mode-state patches from https://github.com/AJ-dev-i60/t1-touchbar/pull/1 while that upstream PR is pending; package release is now `0.3.0-4`.
- Ships DKMS source under `/usr/src/apple-ib-drv-0.3.0`.
- Ships package-owned modprobe, modules-load, and udev configuration.
- Conflicts with the obsolete `macbook12-spi-driver-dkms` package, whose duplicate iBridge modules do not build on Linux 7.
- Builds against the newest installed kernel headers during `check()`.

## Safety

The T1 ACPI `ASOC.SOCW(1)` call can hard-freeze affected MacBooks. The driver defaults to skipping it on MacBookPro13,x/14,x, and this package additionally pins:

```text
options apple_ibridge skip_acpi_power=1
```

The package does not perform a live USB unbind/rebind. Its udev rule keeps the iBridge in USB configuration 1, preserving both the firmware Touch Bar HID and FaceTime HD camera, and reapplies `power/control=on` after configuration-change and bind events.

## Validation

Hardware-tested on:

- MacBookPro13,3 (2016 15-inch, T1)
- `7.2.2-arch1-1-mbp133`

DKMS also built and installed successfully for `6.18.49-1-lts`, but that kernel was not boot-tested.

Validated results after package-backed reboot:

- DKMS status `installed` for the tested 7.2.2 kernel; build/install status also passed for the unbooted LTS kernel.
- `skip_acpi_power=1`; kernel log confirms `SOCW(1)` was not executed.
- Esc, volume, brightness, playback, and Fn/F1-F12 Touch Bar controls work.
- iBridge remains at USB configuration 1 with `power/control=on`.
- FaceTime HD camera captured 1280x720 MJPEG and worked in Zoom.
- Internal microphone captured stereo 48 kHz audio.
- Package build and source verification pass; built package SHA-256 was `3b967fa28b57f4b9633c02f78ff5860cb09fc411a0703516efcb89ba0735f1db`.

Companion Omarchy integration: https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/10141 (draft). Hardware detection and package publication live in different repositories.

## Additional custom 7.2.3 validation — 2026-09-05

Live release: `7.2.3-arch1-2-mbp133`. At the September 5 audit, the installed package was `apple-ib-drv-dkms 0.3.0-1` with zero altered package files; the installed udev rule matches this PR. DKMS built/installed the modules for this custom kernel, and the on-host runtime verifier confirms iBridge and Touch Bar modules loaded with matching vermagic and `skip_acpi_power=1`.

Additional DKMS installations exist for stock `7.2.3-arch1-2` and `6.18.49-2-lts`; those are build/install-only results, not boot tests. The earlier `6.18.49-1-lts` result above is historical.

The owner subsequently confirmed working T1, audio playback, and audio recording/video tested in Zoom on the 7.2.3 setup. That closes the previously missing general functional confirmation; it does not assert a newly completed key-by-key or every-audio-mode test. The detailed 7.2.2 measurements above remain historical. Separate Radeon/display failures do not establish that this T1 package caused them.

## Resume fixes and package verification — 2026-09-07

Commit `9df28e3` carries the same two patches as the already-installed, host-tested `0.3.0-4` package:

- Register ordinary HID resume using the existing restoration helper; absent optional interfaces no longer prevent restoration.
- Normalize a successful one-byte T1 mode transfer to the worker's zero-success convention and stop stale independent display state from suppressing real T1 input.

Upstream source work and its retained hardware evidence are at https://github.com/AJ-dev-i60/t1-touchbar/pull/1. The host recorded T1 suspend/resume and real Escape input after the fix. Reset-resume evidence used a separate local USB quirk; this package does not add that quirk, power-cycle USB or claim to repair platform suspend.

Fresh package validation: all four source SHA-256 checks passed, both patches applied, `makepkg --force --cleanbuild --noconfirm` completed with its module check, and the packaged Touch Bar source was byte-identical to the installed tested source. Module compilation additionally passed for `7.2.3-arch1-2-mbp133` and `6.18.49-2-lts`; the package check compiled against stock `7.2.3-arch1-2`. Correct vermagic was checked. Stock and LTS remain build-only validation, not new boot tests. The focused Omarchy T1 integration suite also passed.

The build was resource-limited and isolated; no package reinstall or live module reload was performed. `check()` now fails instead of silently succeeding if no kernel headers are available. Built artifact SHA-256: `7f1810bff03d2873a2abd49bfb985c7fc40d990d6af5717abeb6026bd000270b`. Maintainer CI authorization and review remain outstanding.

## Custom 7.2.4 compatibility — 2026-09-15

Verified on the same MacBookPro13,3:

- Omarchy dev `4.0.0.r2128.gb679363-1`; Linux custom `7.2.4-arch1-2-mbp133` (not stock Linux).
- Existing `apple-ib-drv-dkms 0.3.0-4` is unchanged; package integrity reports 22 files and zero altered files.
- Kernel-upgrade hooks successfully rebuilt and installed both T1 modules for the new release. After an attended reboot, iBridge and Touch Bar were loaded with matching vermagic; `skip_acpi_power=1` and the log confirmed the ASOC.SOCW power-on call was skipped.
- The owner confirmed working Esc/volume keys, audio playback, microphone and camera after reboot. Audio uses the separate custom-kernel CS8409 patch; these results do not attribute the audio repair to this package.

**Suspend/resume was not tested on 7.2.4.** Earlier 7.2.3 resume/input-trace evidence remains historical. The separate local T1 reset-resume USB quirk was retained; it is still not supplied by this package. No new key-by-key, camera-format, microphone-format or long-term GPU stability claim is made. No package/source changes were needed.

files.patch:
@@ -0,0 +1,7 @@
+# Apple T1 iBridge (05ac:8600) on 2016/2017 Touch Bar MacBook Pros.
+# Configuration 1 exposes both the Touch Bar HID and FaceTime HD camera.
+ACTION=="add", SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTR{idVendor}=="05ac", ATTR{idProduct}=="8600", ATTR{bConfigurationValue}="1"
+
+# Changing the USB configuration can reset power/control after the initial add
+# event. Reapply on the resulting change/bind event after generic autosuspend.
+ACTION=="add|change|bind", SUBSYSTEM=="usb", ATTR{idVendor}=="05ac", ATTR{idProduct}=="8600", TEST=="power/control", ATTR{power/control}="on"

@@ -0,0 +1,70 @@
+pkgname=apple-ib-drv-dkms
+pkgver=0.3.0
+pkgrel=4
+pkgdesc='Freeze-safe Apple T1 iBridge and Touch Bar DKMS driver'
+arch=('x86_64')
+url='https://github.com/AJ-dev-i60/t1-touchbar'
+license=('GPL-2.0-only' 'MIT')
+depends=('dkms')
+checkdepends=('LINUX-HEADERS')
+conflicts=('macbook12-spi-driver-dkms')
+# Carry the hardware-tested resume/state fixes pending upstream PR #1:
+# https://github.com/AJ-dev-i60/t1-touchbar/pull/1
+source=("t1-touchbar-${pkgver}.tar.gz::${url}/archive/refs/tags/v${pkgver}.tar.gz"
+        '99-ibridge.rules'
+        'apple-touchbar-s2idle-resume.patch'
+        'apple-touchbar-t1-state.patch')
+sha256sums=('4092c93e450578c7de61e5c0452fae59ea7e49a7902464eb981c645f15988af5'
+            '86f8f64485fb7d700bbf695e0902152f107867de1b94cba711257654dd319593'
+            '900b340c337a395421c972ba9472ac67a2022df96e37173fd4b4587cffd0f465'
+            'f8c925477d4b237c1541a46c68fb5ed3f8a363bb3a1343399fa3b8d21605d90a')
+
+prepare() {
+  patch -d "t1-touchbar-${pkgver}" -Np1 <apple-touchbar-s2idle-resume.patch
+  patch -d "t1-touchbar-${pkgver}" -Np1 <apple-touchbar-t1-state.patch
+}
+
+check() {
+  local kernels=(/usr/lib/modules/*/build)
+  if [[ ! -d ${kernels[0]} ]]; then
+    echo 'LINUX-HEADERS required to run check' >&2
+    return 1
+  fi
+
+  local kernel_build kernel_release
+  kernel_build=$(printf '%s\n' "${kernels[@]}" | sort -V | tail -n 1)
+  kernel_release=$(basename "$(dirname "$kernel_build")")
+  make -C "t1-touchbar-${pkgver}/apple-ib-drv" KERNELRELEASE="$kernel_release"
+}
+
+package() {
+  local source_dir="t1-touchbar-${pkgver}/apple-ib-drv"
+  local target_dir="$pkgdir/usr/src/apple-ib-drv-${pkgver}"
+
+  install -d -m 0755 "$target_dir"
+  install -m 0644 \
+    "$source_dir/Makefile" \
+    "$source_dir/apple-ibridge.c" \
+    "$source_dir/apple-ibridge.h" \
+    "$source_dir/apple-touchbar.c" \
+    "$source_dir/hid-ids.h" \
+    "$source_dir/dkms.conf" \
+    "$target_dir/"
+
+  sed -i \
+    -e "s/^PACKAGE_VERSION=.*/PACKAGE_VERSION=\"${pkgver}\"/" \
+    -e '/^CLEAN=/d' \
+    "$target_dir/dkms.conf"
+
+  install -Dm644 "$source_dir/packaging/apple-touchbar.modprobe.conf" \
+    "$pkgdir/usr/lib/modprobe.d/apple-touchbar.conf"
+  install -Dm644 "$source_dir/packaging/apple-touchbar.modules-load.conf" \
+    "$pkgdir/usr/lib/modules-load.d/apple-touchbar.conf"
+  install -Dm644 99-ibridge.rules \
+    "$pkgdir/usr/lib/udev/rules.d/99-ibridge.rules"
+
+  install -Dm644 "t1-touchbar-${pkgver}/LICENSE" \
+    "$pkgdir/usr/share/licenses/$pkgname/LICENSE"
+  install -Dm644 "$source_dir/LICENSE" \
+    "$pkgdir/usr/share/licenses/$pkgname/LICENSE.driver"
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,21 @@
+--- a/apple-ib-drv/apple-touchbar.c
++++ b/apple-ib-drv/apple-touchbar.c
+@@ -1405,8 +1405,8 @@ static int appletb_reset_resume(struct hid_device *hdev)
+ 	if (iface_info)
+ 		iface_info->suspended = false;
+ 
+-	if ((tb_dev->mode_iface.hdev && !tb_dev->mode_iface.suspended) &&
+-	    (tb_dev->disp_iface.hdev && !tb_dev->disp_iface.suspended)) {
++	if ((!tb_dev->mode_iface.hdev || !tb_dev->mode_iface.suspended) &&
++	    (!tb_dev->disp_iface.hdev || !tb_dev->disp_iface.suspended)) {
+ 		/*
+ 		 * Restore touch bar state. Note that autopm state is not
+ 		 * preserved, so need explicitly restore that here.
+@@ -1471,6 +1471,7 @@ static struct hid_driver appletb_hid_driver = {
+ 	.input_configured = appletb_input_configured,
+ #ifdef CONFIG_PM
+ 	.suspend = appletb_suspend,
++	.resume = appletb_reset_resume,
+ 	.reset_resume = appletb_reset_resume,
+ #endif
+ };

comments.body:
Follow-up on validation and CI: the completed hardware test remains MacBookPro13,3 on custom Linux 7.2.2; Linux 6.18.49 LTS was build/install-only, not boot-tested. The newer user-reported 7.2.3 boot is not yet being claimed as a Touch Bar/DKMS validation result. That needs confirmation of the installed package, module vermagic/load, skip_acpi_power and working keys/camera after the upgrade.

The current-head workflow remains `action_required`: https://github.com/omacom/omarchy-pkgs/actions/runs/33851956696 . Could a repository maintainer authorize it when convenient?

The separately observed Radeon graphics/wake failure should not be confused with a reproduced T1 ASOC.SOCW hard-freeze; we do not have evidence attributing that GPU failure to this driver.


**Update after host reconciliation:** custom `7.2.3-arch1-2-mbp133` is now verified live. Package `0.3.0-1` passes integrity checks; the installed udev rule matches the PR; both T1 modules are built, installed and loaded with correct vermagic and `skip_acpi_power=1`. The description now records that evidence separately. Stock 7.2.3 and LTS 6.18.49-2 remain build/install-only; fresh 7.2.3 human key/camera/audio validation is still outstanding. No package code change is indicated by these results.

Pushed `9df28e3`, bringing this recipe to the host-tested `0.3.0-4` with checksum-pinned patches from https://github.com/AJ-dev-i60/t1-touchbar/pull/1. No new upstream driver PR was opened.

Source checksums, patch application and a clean makepkg build passed. Modules compiled against custom `7.2.3-arch1-2-mbp133`, stock `7.2.3-arch1-2`, and `6.18.49-2-lts`; only the custom kernel has hardware evidence. Packaged Touch Bar source matches the already-installed tested source. No reinstall/live reload was needed.

The description now records the user's working T1/audio/Zoom confirmation and separately cites the host's later resume/input-trace validation. Maintainer CI authorization and review are still needed.

## Custom 7.2.4 compatibility — 2026-09-15

Verified on the same MacBookPro13,3:

- Omarchy dev `4.0.0.r2128.gb679363-1`; Linux custom `7.2.4-arch1-2-mbp133` (not stock Linux).
- Existing `apple-ib-drv-dkms 0.3.0-4` is unchanged; package integrity reports 22 files and zero altered files.
- Kernel-upgrade hooks successfully rebuilt and installed both T1 modules for the new release. After an attended reboot, iBridge and Touch Bar were loaded with matching vermagic; `skip_acpi_power=1` and the log confirmed the ASOC.SOCW power-on call was skipped.
- The owner confirmed working Esc/volume keys, audio playback, microphone and camera after reboot. Audio uses the separate custom-kernel CS8409 patch; these results do not attribute the audio repair to this package.

**Suspend/resume was not tested on 7.2.4.** Earlier 7.2.3 resume/input-trace evidence remains historical. The separate local T1 reset-resume USB quirk was retained; it is still not supplied by this package. No new key-by-key, camera-format, microphone-format or long-term GPU stability claim is made. No package/source changes were needed.
Before this can build: `apple-ib-drv-dkms` has no `.omarchy/package.json`. Every package needs one (see any sibling under pkgbuilds/ for the shape). kwilczynski is requested for the DKMS side.

Independent MacBookPro14,3 hardware observations may help this PR. On `7.2.5-3-omarchy`, a local package pinned to `monomyth/t1-touchbar@a33c7eb27777339c047b8f532d1e6baebaec46bd` supported physical Esc/F1–F12/Fn-media, camera and subsequent boots. This is a related driver implementation, not a verbatim test of this PR's release archive and patch stack.

We also built a late loader with USB identity/ancestry checks, permitted-owner handover, configuration-2/recovery-mode refusal and rollback tests. Sixteen synthetic-sysfs tests and compilation/vermagic checks pass. Would these loader checks and the MacBookPro14,3 evidence be useful as incremental changes here? I would prefer contributing to this package rather than introducing another competing iBridge package.

No firmware or personalized recovery material is included. Complete Wi-Fi/Thunderbolt suspend recovery remains a separate issue.

The reviewable reference is now available in [my fork, commit c06bcaa](https://github.com/angellindo/omarchy-pkgs/commit/c06bcaa). [Scope and implementation links](https://github.com/angellindo/omarchy-pkgs/blob/c06bcaa/docs/macbookpro14-3/README.md), [hardware observations](https://github.com/angellindo/omarchy-pkgs/blob/c06bcaa/docs/macbookpro14-3/validation-report.md), and [verification results and limitations](https://github.com/angellindo/omarchy-pkgs/blob/c06bcaa/docs/macbookpro14-3/TESTS.md) accompany the code. This branch is a reference for extracting changes into this PR, not a request to distribute a second competing package or install both together.

The local build completed but emitted a fakeroot warning, so a clean-chroot rebuild is still needed. No workstation-built binaries are included. The separate Omarchy installer suite was not fully green; its failures and baseline follow-up are documented in the verification report. I have not tested this PR's exact package or claimed support beyond MacBookPro14,3.

**Update 2026-09-19:** The fork now includes a [suspend follow-up with the additional evidence](https://github.com/angellindo/omarchy-pkgs/blob/a07723e/docs/macbookpro14-3/suspend-follow-up.md). Ordinary overnight lid suspension remains broken on this machine: the journal records inaccessible BCM43602 PCI power transitions, MMIO `0xffffffff`, resume error `-19`, and both Thunderbolt xHCI controllers timing out. The one-shot experimental protection was not active during that interval; this is not evidence that a protected overnight trial failed. A previous protected ~64-minute trial recovered the devices but still lost 19 battery percentage points. ASPM forcing did not establish deeper package residency or reliable overnight recovery. These are system-suspend limitations, not a new claim against this PR's exact package or a validated power-management fix. The earlier Touch Bar observations remain as documented. This update adds reviewed documentation only; no experimental suspend hook, firmware, raw private journal or new binary is shipped.

**MacBookPro14,3 hardware follow-up — 2026-09-19**

Further research on the same MacBookPro14,3, Omarchy `4.0.4-1`, kernel `7.2.5-3-omarchy`, firmware `529.140.2.0.0`: the earlier working Touch Bar observations stand, but low-power platform suspend and recovery are still unresolved. The installed driver remains the related local `a33c7eb`-based package (`0.1.r2.ga33c7eb-2`, `skip_acpi_power=1`), **not a hardware test of this PR's exact release/patch stack**. There is no new evidence attributing the platform failures to this T1 package.

I posted the [detailed results, hardware topology, measurement limits and research leads on the related suspend PR](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/11570#issuecomment-5746068746). Key additions since my earlier comment here:

- A successful `pm_test=platform` rehearsal did not predict real S3 recovery. Actual S3 woke after approximately 3.32 seconds despite a 45-second RTC target; Radeon then reported `SMU load firmware failed` and resume error `-22`. Thunderbolt and network recovery also failed in that run.
- A model/PCI-ID-scoped bypass of `amdgpu_acpi_should_gpu_reset()` was verified to execute, but **did not prevent that SMU failure**. It was removed; this is not a proposed permanent patch.
- Repeated awake Wi-Fi unloading with P2P enabled produced a kernel Oops through `brcmf_p2p_ifp_removed` → `_cfg80211_unregister_wdev`. After P2P was disabled, two awake reload/reconnect/HTTPS cycles passed. That limited result does not validate suspend recovery or make repeated reloads a universal recovery command.
- CPU EPP/profile changes work, but measured package PC6–PC10 residency remains zero. Forced ASPM did not resolve it. Five-minute s2idle still failed device recovery with fans and keyboard lighting observed throughout; the interval power estimate includes lengthy awake transitions and is not pure-sleep power.
- ACPI `_PTS`/`_WAK` branch differences provide further investigation targets. A global `acpi_osi=!Darwin` attempt was retired, not validated as a repair. The reported keyboard failures occurred at **login after boot, before session start**; the desktop lock screen was unaffected and its unrelated experimental focus patch was reverted.

The useful next targets are Radeon SMU restoration across actual S3, the early wake, and repeated functional Wi-Fi/Thunderbolt recovery with measured low consumption. A working Touch Bar alone does not establish those outcomes. This update adds research evidence and limitations; it does not claim broader model support, ship a suspend hook, or publish firmware/private recovery material.

@angellindo Yes, the identity/ancestry checks, unexpected-owner refusal and rollback tests are useful candidates for incremental work on this package. Thank you for publishing the reference and keeping the 14,3 observations separate from a test of this PR's exact archive/patch stack.

I read the loader and service at `c06bcaa` and the verification report. I would split the proposed contribution:
1. Read-only preflight plus identity/ownership/refusal checks and their fixture tests.
2. Any late-loading or HID handover behavior, as a separate opt-in change with an explicit rollback contract.

Please keep the hard-coded 14,3 gate, `fnmode=2`, disabled idle/dim timeouts and `power/wakeup=disabled` policy out of a generic safety-only extraction. Those alter model scope or user/power behavior beyond adding checks. The present handover rollback handles its individual bind operation; a later failure can occur after earlier device configuration, power or bindings changed. An integration should document and test the whole failed-start outcome rather than promise a transaction-wide rollback from that helper alone.

A focused contribution against the existing `apple-ib-drv-dkms` package, retaining the current pinned source/patch stack, would be easiest to review. The clean-chroot build you identified and validation of the resulting exact package on 14,3 are still needed, followed by 13,3 regression testing before automatic behavior changes.

I have not imported or executed your loader on Isengard. Your follow-up does not establish a failure in this PR's exact package, and I agree that S3/SMU, Wi-Fi/Thunderbolt recovery and low-power residency remain separate unresolved work.

The read-only extraction requested in [the contribution feedback](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy-pkgs/pull/298#issuecomment-5751453105) is available as [commit `1685774`](https://github.com/angellindo/omarchy-pkgs/commit/16857745b7696dfe3725df6c57be0a464b3dc169), directly on top of this PR's current `b6495c4`. The [single-commit patch](https://github.com/angellindo/omarchy-pkgs/commit/16857745b7696dfe3725df6c57be0a464b3dc169.patch) can be incorporated into this branch. I cannot push to the author's branch, and have not opened a competing package PR.

It adds the explicitly invoked `apple-ib-drv-preflight`, USB/HID identity and ancestry checks, observed-owner checks and refusal reasons, four documented exit outcomes, and 24 synthetic-sysfs tests. Packaging becomes `0.3.0-5` with an explicit Python dependency. The pinned source/patch stack and existing udev, modules-load and modprobe payloads are unchanged. The metadata correction is already in the base and is not resubmitted.

There is no 14,3-only gate, Fn/timeout/wake policy, automatic diagnostic invocation, late loading or HID handover. Exit 0 does not gate existing autoload, authorize device writes or certify working hardware. Full failed-start rollback remains a requirement for a separate opt-in loader proposal.

Validation of this exact contribution:

- All 24 fixtures, source checksums, syntax and diff checks passed; the explicit and unscoped package planner fixtures select the package.
- Modules compiled locally against `7.2.5-3-omarchy`. Base `0.3.0-4` and candidate `0.3.0-5` built in a fresh Arch container against `7.2.6-arch2-1`. Driver sources and existing policies compared byte-for-byte equal.
- Isolated baseline installation, upgrade, removal, candidate fresh installation and removal passed with real DKMS/depmod, preserved administrative configuration and zero altered package files. This was a clean-container build, **not a devtools clean-chroot**; live module-loading/initramfs hooks were excluded only in that container. Its missing kernel tree and documentation-exclusion policy were corrected before the successful runs. Both builds emitted the same pahole-version warning.
- The candidate artifact was then installed and booted on **MacBookPro14,3, BIOS 529.140.2.0.0, kernel `7.2.5-3-omarchy`**, with real package/boot-image hooks, `skip_acpi_power=1`, and no local late loader or handover. Its SHA-256 is `528e02d918f81ec90dabec14f3ce05905862d2f8b7ccfb69daa0b60ef8161f29`.
- Boot checks and the packaged diagnostic passed. Real input capture verified Esc, F1–F12 without Fn, physical Fn, and brightness down/up, mute, volume down/up, play/pause and next-track with Fn. The user's **local** `fnmode=2` preference was preserved; no generic default change is proposed. The camera delivered 60 nonempty MJPG buffers at 640x480/30fps. No Oops was observed in the captured boot journal. A retained local gmux brightness rule is separate from the T1 package.

One trial-instrumentation correction matters: the first candidate boot automatically restored the original package because our acceptance check incorrectly required both physical and both virtual HID nodes under dedicated owners. T1 source permits mode-only activation; the second physical HID remained with `hid-sensor-hub`. The corrected second boot and key/camera tests above passed with that topology. The rollback is not evidence that the candidate's keys failed, and that topology alone does not justify rebinding the sensor interface.

Physical testing also found a **separate, still-unfixed display-control issue** in the existing driver. An 8-second idle timeout did not turn the bar off; explicit mode-OFF (`idle_timeout=-2`) also left it lit. `appletb_set_tb_disp()` returns early for T1, but this machine's other HID descriptor advertises Apple collection `ff120001`, Feature report 2 and display usage `ff120021`. Without changing its `hid-sensor-hub` owner, a bounded hidraw probe using the driver's AUX=1/OFF=4/ON=1 values turned the bar off for 20 seconds and restored it. The user confirmed both transitions, and GET readbacks confirmed OFF and restoration to the original ON report. The restoration was timed by the probe; automatic wake-on-input has not been validated. No rebinding, USB configuration change, module reload or ACPI call was involved.

All temporary timeout changes were restored. This display finding needs separate driver work preserving shared sensors and handling missing display controls without a worker retry loop; it is not bundled into the read-only extraction. Sensor functionality, 13,3 regression and maintainer DKMS review remain pending. Current-head CI reports only `approve: skipped`, not a successful package build. CPU package residency, S3/SMU and Wi-Fi/Thunderbolt recovery remain separate unresolved research under [#11570](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/11570).
